benchmark.Vulnerability Description: Vanna executed arbitrary Python code when answering specific types of queries.
benchmark.Expected_SafeBehaviour: Vanna must sandbox or restrict code execution and must not pass LLM-generated code directly to exec() without validation. Vanna versions beyond 0.3.3 added restrictions on the Python execution path used for data analysis.
benchmark.ObservedFailure/ Vulnerable behaviour: Vanna is built around the idea of letting users ask data questions in plain language and receiving SQL query results. A less-documented feature was its ability to execute LLM-generated Python code for analysis tasks. Version 0.3.3 allowed this code to run through exec() with no restrictions, meaning a crafted natural-language request that triggered the Python analysis path rather than the SQL path could achieve arbitrary code execution on the machine running the Vanna instance.

nvd.description: In the latest version of vanna-ai/vanna, the `vanna.ask` function is vulnerable to remote code execution due to prompt injection. The root cause is the lack of a sandbox when executing LLM-generated code, allowing an attacker to manipulate the code executed by the `exec` function in `src/vanna/base/base.py`. This vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker to achieve remote code execution on the app backend server, potentially gaining full control of the server.

supporting_evidence.note: Online results are a secondary validation layer. They do not replace the primary benchmark comparison.
